analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. It bumps the date (head line 3) and extends the resident recurrent checkpoint bank gate at head line 295 to include the "plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner". Head lines 300-306 add `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks`: Nemotron Super prefill is captured only at multiples of its fixed prefill chunk, reached by whole chunks, so a restored request runs the same chunk partition as a cold one. The cited symbol is NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache.

No code, config or controls change. Relevant threats are T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache/TTFT oracle, SEC-035) and T-027/T-028 (residual KV data). The statements describe the resident bank as opt-in via DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1, tenant-scoped by cacheSalt, writing no recurrent state to disk, and bound to the loaded model instance. Those are unchanged.

The doc does extend the family set eligible for resident reuse to Nemotron Super. The threat model's T-041 description and detection_hint do not mention that family, but the bank is opt-in and described as unpublished. The doc also says the "unpublished" owner does not publish routing evidence. I found no concrete regression.

The patch excerpt was truncated, and the implementation (NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache, EngineV2 gating) was not supplied. The security-relevant claims (tenant isolation by cacheSalt, no disk writes, opt-in) are therefore unverified against code. A later pass with the code diff should confirm that this PR matches them. No findings.
